playbook.intent: A new quarter is about to open while the roadmap is still a set of half-agreed opinions held separately at company, product and squad level. It closes when the roadmap is published, every squad objective ladders up to a company one, the chosen bets have reserved capacity behind them, and the list of what the quarter will deliberately not do is written where the people who asked for those things can read it.
playbook.scope: Quarter starts with a published roadmap, OKRs cascaded from company → product → squad level, prioritised bets locked, capacity reserved, and a written 'what we are NOT doing' anti-roadmap.

success-criteria.criterion: A dated roadmap for the quarter is published somewhere every person who will be asked about it can reach without requesting access
Every squad objective traces upward to a product objective and a company objective, leaving no orphan at any level
The prioritised bets were ranked against each other by a stated scoring method, not by whoever argued longest in the room
Reserved capacity is written beside each bet, and the total does not exceed the hours the squads actually have after run-the-business work
The anti-roadmap names what will not be done this quarter and who requested each of those things, so the answer is on paper before they ask again
Every key result reads off a data source that already exists, so scoring at quarter end needs no new instrumentation built first
Anyone who lost a prioritisation argument has the reasoning in writing rather than only the outcome
